The '''2005 FA Community Shield''' (also known as '''The FA Community Shield in partnership with [[McDonald's]]''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 83rd staging of the [[FA Community Shield]], an annual football match contested by the reigning champions of the [[Premier League]] and the holders of the [[FA Cup]]. It was held at the [[Millennium Stadium]] in [[Cardiff]] on 7 August 2005. The game was played between [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], champions of the [[2004–05 FA Premier League|2004–05 Premier League]] and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], who beat [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] to win the [[2005 FA Cup Final]]. Chelsea won the match 2–1 in front of a crowd of 58,014.

This was Chelsea's fifth Community Shield appearance to Arsenal's 19th. Relations between the two clubs were hostile before the match, given Chelsea's illicit attempts to sign Arsenal defender [[Ashley Cole]]. In the game Chelsea took the lead when striker [[Didier Drogba]] scored in the eighth minute. He scored again in the second half, before [[Cesc Fàbregas]] replied for Arsenal with a goal in the 64th minute. [[José Mourinho]] praised Chelsea in his post-match interview and felt the team looked comfortable in defence. Opposing manager [[Arsène Wenger]] admitted Drogba had presented problems for Arsenal and likened his opponents to a [[long ball]] team, who on the day played "very direct".

==Background and pre-match==
Founded in 1908 as a successor to the [[Sheriff of London Charity Shield]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Abandonment of the Sheriff Shield |page=11 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=19 April 1908}}</ref> the [[FA Community Shield]] began as a contest between the respective champions of the [[The Football League|Football League]] and [[Southern Football League|Southern League]], although in 1913, it was played between an Amateurs XI and a Professionals XI.<ref>{{cite news |title=The F.A. Charity Shield |page=10 |newspaper=The Times |date=7 October 1913}}</ref> In 1921, it was played by the league champions of the top division and [[FA Cup]] winners for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Peter |last=Ferguson |title=The Shield: From the beginning |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110830223116/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/News/Team-news/2011/August/Community-Shield-2011/The-Shield-from-the-beginning |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=4 August 2011 |access-date=21 April 2014 |archive-date=30 August 2011}}</ref>{{#tag:ref|The [[Premier League]] replaced the [[Football League First Division]] at the top of the [[English football league system|English football pyramid]] after its inception in 1992.<ref>{{cite news |title=Continental or the full English? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/dec/02/sport.sportfeatures |first=Alex |last=Fynn |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=2 December 2001 |access-date=3 July 2014}}</ref>|group=lower-alpha}} Cardiff's [[Millennium Stadium]] was hosting the Shield for the fifth time; it took over as the venue for the event while [[Wembley Stadium]] underwent a six-year renovation between 2001 and 2006.<ref name="faru">{{cite web|title=The FA Community Shield history |url=http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=3 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609184712/http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |archive-date=9 June 2013 |url-status=live  }}</ref>

Chelsea qualified for the 2005 FA Community Shield as winners of the [[2004–05 FA Premier League]]. It was their first league title in 50 years, remembered for the records broken such as the most wins, fewest goals conceded in a league season and most points accumulated.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea ease into record books |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/11/match.manchesterunited |first=Kevin |last=McCarra |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=11 May 2005 |access-date=18 May 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=2004–05 Season Review |url=http://www.premierleague.com/history/2004-05 |publisher=Premier League |access-date=19 July 2016 |archive-date=11 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160711050416/http://www.premierleague.com/history/2004-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The other Community Shield place went to Arsenal, who beat [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] to win the [[2005 FA Cup Final|final]] of the [[2004–05 FA Cup]]. Arsenal was making its 19th Community Shield appearance and held the Shield after beating Manchester United 3–1 [[2004 FA Community Shield|a year previously]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.statto.com/football/stats/england/community-shield/honours |title=English Community Shield: Honours |publisher=Statto Organisation |access-date=21 May 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140713124226/http://www.statto.com/football/stats/england/community-shield/honours |archive-date=13 July 2014 }}</ref> By contrast this was Chelsea's fifth appearance, their first since [[2000 FA Charity Shield|2000]].<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |title=England – List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation (RSSSF) |date=15 August 2013 |access-date=2 April 2014 |first=James |last=Ross}}</ref> It was also the first meeting between both sides in the Shield.<ref name="rsssf"/>

Chelsea manager [[José Mourinho]] described relations between the two clubs as "non-existent", given his club's approach to sign ([[tapping up]]) Arsenal defender [[Ashley Cole]].<ref name="pmm">{{cite news |last=Wiechula |first=Frank |title=Wenger's Guns aim at Kenyon |date=7 August 2005 |newspaper=The People |location=London |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/wengers-guns-aim-at-kenyon-1609790 |access-date=29 May 2014}}</ref> The player had met Mourinho and chief executive [[Peter Kenyon]] at a London hotel in January 2005, without Arsenal's consent.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tapping-up row that ran and ran |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2360492/Tapping-up-row-that-ran-and-ran.html |first=Christopher |last=Davies |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=2 June 2005 |access-date=25 May 2014}}</ref> Chelsea, Mourinho and Cole were all later found guilty by an independent commission and fined accordingly; the club was charged the most amount – [[Pound sterling|£]]300,000.<ref>{{cite news |title=Record fines will not cut off tap at source |first=Matt |last=Dickinson |page=95 |newspaper=The Times |date=2 June 2005}}</ref>

The ownership of Chelsea by Russian billionaire [[Roman Abramovich]] also caused friction between both clubs. Arsenal manager [[Arsène Wenger]] said in May 2005: "They are a financially doped club. They have enhancement of performances through financial resources which are unlimited. For me, it's a kind of doping because it's not in any way linked to their resources. It puts pressure on the market that is not very healthy. They can go to [[Steven Gerrard]] or [[Rio Ferdinand]] and 'say how much do you earn, we'll give you twice as much.'"<ref>{{cite news |title=Mourinho's X-Files |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/4398956.stm |work=BBC Sport |date=2 November 2005 |access-date=29 May 2014}}</ref> Wenger admitted this put Arsenal at a disadvantage in the [[transfer market]]; in the case of [[Shaun Wright-Phillips]], a long-term target, Chelsea's interest meant Arsenal needed to wait before making a bid.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wenger faces Wright-Phillips wait |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/arsenal/4669433.stm |work=BBC Sport |date=11 July 2005 |access-date=29 May 2014}}</ref> The player eventually joined Chelsea from [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] for £21 million.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wright-Phillips signs for Chelsea |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4621425.stm |work=BBC Sport |date=18 July 2005 |access-date=29 May 2014}}</ref>

==Match==

===Team selection===
Chelsea fielded a full-strength team, which lined up in a [[Formation (association football)#4.E2.80.933.E2.80.933|4–3–3]] formation; an attacking three of [[Didier Drogba]], [[Damien Duff]] and [[Arjen Robben]].<ref name="ctn">{{cite web|url=https://review.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/861943 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140701142133/http://review.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/861943 |url-status=dead |archive-date=1 July 2014 |title=Community Shield team news: Chelsea v Arsenal |publisher=Chelsea Football Club |date=7 August 2005 |access-date=18 May 2014 }}</ref> [[Asier Del Horno]] was named as left back, which meant [[William Gallas]] moved to central defence.<ref name="ctn"/> Wright-Phillips began the match on the substitute bench.<ref name="ctn"/> Arsenal's line up by contrast was relatively inexperienced in midfield – [[Gilberto Silva]] was on the bench and [[Mathieu Flamini]] partnered [[Cesc Fàbregas]] in the centre. Up front [[Dennis Bergkamp]] started alongside striker [[Thierry Henry]].<ref name="ctn"/> The team played in a [[Formation (association football)#4–4–2|4–4–2]] formation.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal |page=S11 |newspaper=The Times |date=8 August 2005}}</ref>

===Summary===
[[File:CHELSEA v arsenal - Community Shield 2005 (401045836) (2).jpg|thumb|upright|250px|Action during the match]]
The stadium observed a period of silence in memory of the victims of the [[7 July 2005 London bombings|July bombings in London]], and a mark of respect to Arsenal fan [[Murder of Anthony Walker|Anthony Walker]], killed on Merseyside the previous week.<ref>{{cite web |title=Silence observed for murdered fan |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/merseyside/4127742.stm |work=BBC News |date=6 August 2005 |access-date=19 July 2016}}</ref> Arsenal in their away strip of yellow kicked off the match; they won a corner after four minutes, but their threat was averted by Chelsea.<ref name="clock">{{cite news |title=Clockwatch: Chelsea 2–1 Arsenal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/4129288.stm |work=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2005 |access-date=30 December 2013}}</ref> In the eighth minute Del Horno hit a long pass to the edge of Arsenal's right area. Drogba controlled the ball with his chest and went beyond his marker [[Philippe Senderos]]. He shot the ball past goalkeeper [[Jens Lehmann]] in the Arsenal goal to give Chelsea a 1–0 lead.<ref name="gur">{{cite news |title=Drogba power delivers the early prize |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/aug/08/match.sport11 |first=Kevin |last=McCarra |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=8 August 2005 |access-date=29 May 2014}}</ref> Arsenal began to dominate proceedings, but struggled to make use of their advantage.<ref name="clock"/> A slip by Senderos in the 20th minute invited Robben to make a run down the right side of the pitch, but the chance for Chelsea was brief as Senderos won the ball back.<ref name="clock"/> Four minutes later Fàbregas and [[Claude Makélélé]] were each shown a yellow card for clashing with one another.<ref name="clock"/> Arsenal in the 36th minute fashioned their best chance of the game through [[Kolo Touré]], whose shot forced goalkeeper [[Petr Čech]] to save acrobatically.<ref name="ssr">{{cite news |title=Chelsea lift Community Shield |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/61666/report |publisher=Sky Sports |first=Patrick |last=Goss |date=7 August 2005 |access-date=14 January 2013}}</ref> Six minutes before the interval Drogba was ruled offside, but continued to run in the direction of Arsenal's goal. He went down on a challenge from Lauren and proceeded to roll around Arsenal's penalty area once Lehmann got involved – the "farce" was brought to a close after words from the referee.<ref name="clock"/>

Arsenal made a host of changes before the match restarted – Gilberto, [[Robin van Persie]] and [[Alexander Hleb]] were substituted on for Bergkamp, [[Robert Pires]] and Flamini.<ref>{{cite news |title=Drogba's double spells trouble |first=Matt |last=Dickinson |pages=S10-11 |newspaper=The Times |date=8 August 2005}}</ref> Robben made a run down the right side of the pitch, but failed to get past Senderos in what was the first notable action of the second half.<ref name="clock"/> Moments after, [[Freddie Ljungberg]]'s attempt on goal was cleared by the Chelsea defence following good play by Van Persie.<ref name="clock"/> In the 57th minute Chelsea increased their lead. A long pass found Drogba, who once more held off Senderos in pursuit of the ball. He was forced wide by Lehmann, but on the turn shot the ball through the net to score his second goal of the game.<ref name="gur"/> Drogba was then replaced by [[Hernán Crespo]], and [[Tiago Mendes|Tiago]] came on for [[Eiður Guðjohnsen]].<ref name="clock"/> Arsenal scored in the 64th minute; Ljungberg crossed the ball from the left and Fàbregas evaded the Chelsea defence to slot it past Čech in the goal.<ref name="ssr"/> Both clubs made mass substitutions in the final third of the game, notably Wright-Phillips coming on for his Chelsea debut in place of Robben.<ref name="clock"/> Arsenal continued to push for an equaliser the longer the match went on, which meant they were culpable to Chelsea countering. A free-kick by Van Persie was saved by Čech and it was not until the 86th minute that Henry fashioned his first chance of the half – it too was dealt with by Čech.<ref name="clock"/> Chelsea continued to withstand Arsenal's pressure in injury time and came close to scoring a third goal, but for Touré's intervention.<ref name="clock"/>

==Post-match and aftermath==
{{Quote box|width=260px|bgcolor=#c6dbf7|align=right|quote= "Our strength is that we can mix it up. We can play football, or we can ask for a longer ball. Playing a long-ball game does not mean you show a lack of quality. We have different qualities – that is one of our strengths."|salign = left |source=[[Frank Lampard]] on Chelsea's playing style.<ref name="lamps">{{cite news |title=Lampard says Wenger is rattled by Chelsea |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/lampard-says-wenger-is-rattled-by-chelsea-502436.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/lampard-says-wenger-is-rattled-by-chelsea-502436.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |first=Jason |last=Burt |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=12 August 2005 |access-date=29 December 2013}}{{cbignore}}</ref>}}

Mourinho believed his team deserved to win and said after scoring the first goal, "we looked comfortable and solid in the defence and good on the counter-attack."<ref name="mo">{{cite web |title=Smiles on our faces |url=http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2005/07/CS2005_JoseMourinho_Reaction.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20051112115149/http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2005/07/CS2005_JoseMourinho_Reaction.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 November 2005 |publisher=The Football Association |date=7 August 2005 |access-date=30 December 2013 }}</ref> He did not believe the result would have any consequences for either team, but said "...it is better to win than to lose and we can go home happy and with a smile on our faces."<ref name="mo"/> [[John Terry]] described the victory as a "perfect start", and added it gave Chelsea a psychological edge over Arsenal.<ref name="mour">{{cite news |title=Chelsea boss hails winning effort |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/4747703.stm |work=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2005 |access-date=30 December 2013}}</ref> Drogba felt the result was good for the team's confidence, though confessed Chelsea did not play well – particularly in midfield.<ref name="mour"/>

Two weeks after the Community Shield match, both teams played each other in the league at Chelsea's home ground, [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]].<ref>{{cite news |title=The Weekend's Fixtures |page=81 |newspaper=The Times |date=20 August 2005}}</ref> Drogba scored the only goal of the game, which marked Arsenal's first league defeat against their opponents in ten years.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea 1–0 Arsenal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4148530.stm |work=BBC Sport |date=21 August 2005 |access-date=29 December 2013}}</ref> Chelsea also beat Arsenal away from home on their last visit to Highbury, later in December, and went on to retain the Premier League.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea raise their game to leave Wenger alone in despondency |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/dec/19/match.sport11 |first=Kevin |last=McCarra |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=19 December 2005 |access-date=30 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Clinical Chelsea expose Ferguson's blind faith |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/may/01/match.sport5 |first=Kevin |last=McCarra |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=1 May 2006 |access-date=30 December 2013}}</ref> 

At odds with their indifferent league form which led them to a narrowly earned 4th place finish (outside of the top two for the first time under coach Arsene Wenger), Arsenal's performances in the [[UEFA Champions League]] were appreciable. They became the first London team to participate in a [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] [[2006 UEFA Champions League final|final]], though lost 2–1 to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] at the [[Stade de France]] in Saint-Denis.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gunners to rake in the riches after Spanish survival |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/apr/26/championsleague200506.championsleague |first=Matt |last=Scott |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=26 April 2006 |access-date=30 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Valiant Arsenal fall at the last |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/may/18/match.championsleague |first=Kevin |last=McCarra |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=18 May 2006 |access-date=30 December 2013}}</ref>
